# Generated files

Know which generated paths and names you can import, and which files to ignore.

## Public paths

| Path | What it holds | Stable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sdk/index.js` | The client and its types | Yes |
| `sdk/models/<Name>.js` | One runtime model class per object schema | Yes |
| `sdk/operations/<name>.js` | One operation factory per endpoint | Yes |
| `<name>.model.generated.ts` | The generated base beside each model file | Yes |
| `<models.output>/<package name>/<name>.model.generated.ts` | The generated base of a shared model file | Yes |
| `golem.yaml` | Your configuration keys | Yes |

The SDK folder is the `sdk` output that you configure. Import only from the paths above.

## Ignore or commit generated files {#gitignore}

Golem needs no generated file in git. `golem build` generates first, so a fresh clone builds with one command. You choose whether to commit the generated files:

- **Ignore them.** Put them in `.gitignore`. Run `golem generate` or `golem build` in CI. Your editor needs one `golem generate`, or a running `golem watch`, to see the generated files.
- **Commit them.** A review then shows the generated changes. Run `golem check` in CI, so that a stale generated file fails the run.

Put `.golem/` in `.gitignore` in both cases. To ignore the generated files, add their paths:

```text
.golem/
*.generated.ts
src/generated/
sdk/
```

`.golem/` holds the state of golem on your machine. Any run of `golem generate`, `golem build` or `golem watch` writes it again. A model suffix such as `.entity.mts` or `.entity.cts` makes `.generated.mts` or `.generated.cts` files. Add a line for each extension that your suffixes use.

Add every other generated path by name: the OpenAPI document that a `controllers` job writes, and the files of a `generators` job. A tool that imports such a file needs it generated first, so run `golem generate` before it.

The OpenAPI document of a `controllers` job is a generated file. When you ignore it, it reaches the projects that read it through a run of the project that owns it:

- `golem generate` or `golem build` in the owning project writes the document again.
- A project that reads the document sets it as the `input` of an `openapi` job. Run `golem generate` in the owning project first ([SDK types in your models](/guide/models-and-client#configure-both-generators)). In one `golem.yaml`, an `openapi` job after the controllers job needs no first run.
- In CI, run `golem generate` or `golem build` in the owning project before the steps of a project that reads the document.
- `golem check` fails when the document is missing or differs from the document that the controllers job writes. It writes nothing ([check](/reference/cli#generate-and-check)).

## Default locations

| Output | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Model files | `src/generated/models/`, below the `root` of the models job |
| Operation codecs | `src/generated/operation-codecs.ts`, below the `root` of the controllers job |
| OpenAPI document and SDK | The paths you configure |

`models.output` overrides the model location. The operation codecs path is fixed.

## Generated names

Each `<name>.model.generated.ts` file is public for the models that its source declares. `<Alias>` is the exact type alias.

| Name | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<Alias>BaseModel` | The class that your class extends, for an `IModel` |
| `<Alias>Fields` | Field values, with nested model instances |
| `<Alias>Init` | Constructor input |
| `<Alias>JSON` | The plain data that `toWireFormat` returns |
| `parse<Alias>`, `stringify<Alias>`, `validate<Alias>`, `assert<Alias>`, `toWireFormat<Alias>`, `fromWireFormat<Alias>` | Functions for the model |

`type TPayment = IModel<…>` gives `TPaymentBaseModel` and `parseTPayment`. `type Payment = IModel<…>` gives `PaymentBaseModel`. `type TPermissionModel = IModel<…>` gives `TPermissionModelBaseModel`. A class links to its model through `extends <Alias>BaseModel` and can have any name. Exports that start with `__golem` are not part of the public API.

Golem writes a generated file beside a model file inside `models.root`. Each app writes the generated file of a [shared model file](/guide/shared-models#where-each-app-writes) in its own `models.output`. The models job skips a discovered model file that has no `IModel` or `IObject` alias. A file that `models.sources` names is never skipped ([rules](/reference/config#typescript-models)).

The first line of a generated model file names the version of golem that wrote it, for example `/* Generated by @exprtlabs/golem-model 1.0.0. Do not edit. */`.

## Generated SDK names

An `openapi` job writes these names for each object schema in `components.schemas`. The table uses the schema `Money`. Another schema gives the same names with its own name in place of `Money`.

| What | Name for `Money` | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JSON data type | `Money`, also `MoneyJSON` | The plain data of the request or response body. |
| Model class | `MoneyModel` | The runtime class. `fromWireFormat<MoneyModel>(data)` returns an instance. |
| Fields and constructor input | `MoneyFields`, `MoneyInit` | The field values of the class, and the input of its constructor. |
| Type check | `validateMoney(value)` | Returns whether `value` matches. It narrows `value` to `MoneyFields`. With validation off, it throws `ValidationUnavailable`. |
| Assertion | `assertMoney(value)` | Throws when `value` does not match. Otherwise it returns `value` as `MoneyFields`. With validation off, it throws `ValidationUnavailable`. |
| Field type in another model | `MoneyModel` | A field that refers to `Money` has this type in `ChargeModel` and in `ChargeFields`. It adds `null` when the schema allows `null`. |
| Other functions | `parseMoney`, `stringifyMoney`, `fromWireFormatMoney`, `toWireFormatMoney`, `encodeMoney` | Functions for the schema. |

The rules for the names:

- The name is the schema key, in PascalCase. Each word starts with a capital letter. A character that is not a letter, a digit, `_` or `$` starts a new word, and so does a capital after a lowercase letter or a digit. `charge` gives `Charge`, `Foo-Bar` gives `FooBar`, and `paymentMethod` gives `PaymentMethod`. `TMoney` stays `TMoney`.
- The suffixes and function prefixes go on that name. A schema `Charge` gives `Charge` and `ChargeModel`. A schema `TMoney` gives `TMoney` and `TMoneyModel`: the name keeps the schema's own prefix.
- A `controllers` job names a schema after its model ([component names](/reference/nestjs#component-names)). `type TMoney = IModel<…>` with no class gives the schema `TMoney`.
- Only an object schema has the class, the fields, the init type, the `JSON` type and the functions. A schema of another type, such as a string enum or an array, has the data type only.
- A `oneOf` union, or an `anyOf` union with a `discriminator`, also gets `<Name>Model` when every variant is an object schema that extends the same base schema through `allOf`. The class is abstract and the variants extend it.
- A variant that two or more unions select cannot extend them all. It extends its base schema, and each of its unions answers `instanceof` for it. The other variants of those unions still extend the union class.

Two schemas that give one name stop generation with a `generated name collision` error. The schemas `Foo-Bar` and `Foo.Bar` both give `FooBar`. The error names both schemas with the place of each in the document. Rename one schema in the document.

The diagnostics for these names:

- [OPENAPI_DISCRIMINATOR_IMPLICIT_VALUE](/reference/diagnostics#openapi-discriminator-implicit-value): a variant with no `mapping` entry is selected by its schema name, not by its generated name.

Call operations with these names in [Call operations](/guide/client-usage#import-one-operation-or-model). Use them as the field types of your own models in [SDK types in your models](/guide/models-and-client).

## Derived type names

A type built from a model, such as `Omit<TMerchant, 'id'>`, gets a schema name from its shape. Names are stable across runs.

| Type | Name |
| --- | --- |
| `Omit<TMerchant, 'id'>` | `TMerchantOmitId` |
| `Pick<TMerchant, 'name' \| 'id'>` | `TMerchantPickIdName` |
| `Partial<Omit<TMerchant, 'id'>>` | `TMerchantOmitIdPartial` |
| `TMerchant & TMoney` | `TMerchantAndTMoney` |
| The `billing` property of `TPayment` | `TPaymentBilling` |

The first matching rule gives the name:

1. An intersection of named models. The sorted names join with `And`.
2. A type alias that names the type, such as `type TBilling = Omit<TMerchant, 'id'>`, which gives `TBilling`. The alias name is used as written. The alias needs no type parameters, must be declared in your own source rather than a `.d.ts` file, and must have an ASCII identifier name.
3. A type that holds itself, such as `interface Tree { kids: Tree[] }` or a class that lists its own kind. It takes the name of its interface, class or type alias, and its inner uses are references to that schema. A name that is not an ASCII identifier gives the type the name that rule 5 gives at its first use.
4. A named model wrapped in up to three levels of `Pick`, `Omit`, `Partial`, `Required` and `Readonly`, each key list with at most three string-literal keys. Keys are sorted and written in PascalCase, innermost wrapper first.
5. Anything else: the owner plus the property, such as `TPayment.billing` giving `TPaymentBilling`. The owner of a model field is the model. The owner of a controller parameter is the controller class name without a trailing `Controller`, the method name, and `Body` or `Query`, such as `PaymentsCreateBody` for `PaymentsController.create`. Other parameters use the parameter name instead. The owner of a controller response ends in `Response`. Underscores and other characters outside letters and digits are dropped and the next letter is capitalized, so `Order_V2` becomes `OrderV2`. A property name that contains a non-ASCII character gives the part `Field`, such as `OrderField`. An owner name that contains a non-ASCII character, or does not start with a letter after cleanup, becomes `Model`, such as `ModelShape`.

When the members of a union fall back to the owner plus the property, each member adds a part:

| Member | Name part |
| --- | --- |
| Every member has a string-literal property, and the values stay different | The PascalCase value of that property, such as `TOrderEitherCard`. If several properties qualify, the first in code-unit order wins. |
| No such property | The position of the member in the union as written, such as `TOrderEither1`. |
| A member that rules 1 to 3 name | It keeps that name. |

A union written through a type alias counts the alias's members in place.

Non-default settings, from the model option or from `golem.yaml`, add suffixes in this order:

| Suffix | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| `Loose` | `exact: false` |
| `Any` | `allowAny: true` |
| `Wire` | The wire representation |

A controllers job always reads the types that a signature spells out, such as an inline body, with `exact: false`, whatever `exact` says in `golem.yaml`. Their derived names end in `Loose`, such as `PaymentsCreateBodyMerchantLoose` for the `merchant` field of an inline body. A model that a signature names keeps its own `exact` and its own name.

Equal shapes from different expressions merge into one schema. The alphabetically first name stays.

Two different shapes that get the same name fail generation with [RUNM1059](/reference/diagnostics#runm1059), as does a derived name that equals a model name. The message names both source locations. Declare a named type alias to choose the name.

## Runtime version

- **Rule:** Install `@exprtlabs/golem` at or above the version of each built-in generator package that the configuration uses, with the same major version. A third-party generator has its own version and is not compared.
- **Check:** `generate`, `check`, `exec`, `watch` and `build` compare the installed `@exprtlabs/golem` with `@exprtlabs/golem-model`, `@exprtlabs/golem-openapi` and `@exprtlabs/golem-ts-openapi`. They fail before they write when the runtime is older or has a different major version. The message names both packages and versions.
